title: P2 — Mesh protocol has no wire-format documentation and several claims are overstated: (a) docs/specs.md lists KeepaliveAck as a federation type but the type does not exist in code (docs drift); (b) README claims a REGISTER/REGISTER_ACK registration handshake — the server never sends REGISTER_ACK (no server-side REGISTER handler exists; client register() is fire-and-forget); (c) KEEPALIVE frames are sent by both sides every 30s but never processed server-side (no liveness effect); (d) response routing keys routes by request message_id but looks them up by response request_id — responders must echo the request's message_id as request_id or the response is silently dropped and the requester times out (hunter live-verified both directions with raw WS clients); (e) malformed frames (bad timestamp type, wrong target shape) are silently dropped with no ERROR frame and no log. Server default CR_WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES=5; agent said 3. README + docs/openapi.yaml document retries (0-10, default 5) as an agent-level knob — it does nothing observable. Same for blocking mode: wb-dead with retries=2 timed out at the deliver-level timeout_ms with status 500, retry count invisible. Fix direction: Make the webhook driver honor agent webhook.retries (or document that CR_WEBHOOK_MAX_RETRIES floors it), and log the configured vs used value.

title: [obs:P1] message path is undebuggable: no request correlation id, zero logging on relay accept + webhook dispatch
detail: Deep-debug audit 2026-09-14: the two hottest events on a message bus — a relay publish accepted and a webhook delivery dispatched — emit ZERO log lines (internal/relay/handler.go: 0 slog calls; internal/webhook/driver.go: 0). There is no request correlation id (X-Request-Id or otherwise), so a 202 in the access log cannot be tied to the later webhook POST, guard decision, or FEDERATION_FAILED notice. Federation is the counter-example: hold.go logs the entire lifecycle (held, retry-persist, recovered, failed) and it is a joy to debug. Fix: (1) middleware generates/propagates X-Request-Id, echoes it on responses, and every slog line in the request path carries it; (2) deliver-202, webhook dispatch + outcome, and guard decision log one line each carrying message_id + agent_id + sender; (3) mesh REGISTER/REQUEST-drop and WS subscribe/unsubscribe lifecycle log at debug level.

title: [P2] PATCH /agents/{id} echoes the pre-write last_seen, and the memory backend never advances it
detail: Worker out-of-scope finding during DF-CRIER-151 (worker c319e6f, live postgres probe /tmp/crier-t268/probe-out.txt): the PATCH /agents/{id} response echoes the PRE-write last_seen. Step 5 (the PATCH, HTTP 200) returns last_seen=2026-09-14T23:19:17.600589-05:00 while step 6 (GET immediately after) returns 2026-09-14T23:19:20.31042-05:00, i.e. the response body is rendered from the caller's in-memory copy rather than from the row that was just written. The in-memory backend is further behind: it never advances last_seen at all on update (Update writes capabilities/webhook/guard only), so a client cannot use last_seen from a PATCH response to confirm the write. No data is lost and delivery is unaffected — this is a wire-contract inconsistency, not the DF-CRIER-151 failure shape. Fix direction: have both stores refresh agent.LastSeen (and the other persisted defaults) on the caller's object before the handler renders the response, with a test asserting the PATCH response's last_seen equals the subsequent GET's.

Also verify whether deliverHarness's TimeoutMs:100 override reaches the client (webhook.Config.TimeoutMs) or only sets the budget. Fix candidates: (a) give the blocking attempt context.WithTimeout(remaining budget) so an attempt can never overrun the budget; (b) harden the test (longer hang, wall-clock assert); (c) check no package-level shared webhook.Client with a short timeout bleeds across tests in the same package. title: [P1] Flake-repro load harness had no bound and no teardown - host locked at loadavg 220-346 for hours (2026-09-18)
detail: ROOT CAUSE of the 2026-09-18 host lock-up (Bane: 'another one of those fork bombs'). The DF-CRIER-252-class repro ('test fails 4/24 runs ON A LOADED BOX') drives a load generator that spawns unbounded busy-wait units: `timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c while :; do :; done`, launched from a `for i in $(seq ...)` loop in /home/kara/crier. MEASURED: 73 -> 278 concurrent units over ~20 min; each burns ~13% CPU (null loop, zero work); combined with the fleet, loadavg hit 220/346/237 with ~2000 processes; the box was effectively unusable for hours. Repeated judge runs (gitreins task complete DF-CRIER-252, judge --run-job job-1b252442...) respawn them, and units are ORPHANED to `systemd --user` (PPID=user manager) when their spawner exits, so they outlive the evaluation that created them (300s lifetime each, unbounded count). No containment existed: user-manager TasksMax=72934 (effectively unlimited). FIX: (1) bound the load in the repro harness - hard max unit count (default <=8), unit lifetime <=30s, try/finally + SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP teardown so no unit outlives its run; (2) never leave orphans: the harness must kill its own process group on exit and on abort; (3) serialize load-class work - one load repro at a time per host, and skip (recorded as SKIPPED with reason) when host loadavg is already above threshold; (4) prefer a bounded load tool over hand-rolled while-loops. FLEET MITIGATION INSTALLED (Kara-agent): ~/.hermes/scripts/forkbomb-reaper.py + forkbomb-reaper.timer (60s) kills busy-wait units older than 120s and logs to ~/.hermes/logs/forkbomb-reaper.jsonl; first run reaped 49 units + their spawner. PENDING (needs root): TasksMax/MemoryMax drop-in on user@1000.service as structural containment.  CORRECTION (same day, after reading the code): `scripts/loadgen.py` is NOT the emitter — it is the already-correct replacement (bounded workers MAX_WORKERS=8, capped seconds, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG so children die with the runner, refuses to run on a shared host, fails the run if any child survives). The actual emitter is AD-HOC, AGENT-AUTHORED shell: agents hand-rolled `for i in $(seq 1 N); do timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c 'while :; do :; done' & done` as a 'load the box' step, with no teardown, so the units were orphaned to systemd --user and outlived every caller (state.db evidence across projects/weeks: Kobayashi-Maru 2026-08-25, ring-runner, crier). FIX LANDED 2026-09-18: the terminal-jail plugin now vetoes this class at the tool boundary (pre_tool_call block directive) via terminal_jail/spin_policy.py — busy-wait loops, unbounded yes/cat /dev/zero/dd burns and shell fork bombs; 5/5 tests pass; deliberate override HERMES_TERMINAL_JAIL_ALLOW_SPIN=1. Remaining scope: make loadgen the easy path for agents (wrapper + AGENTS.md pointer), audit remaining harnesses for the old idiom, keep the host reaper as backstop. NOTE: this row was lost once to a mid-write crash during that same correction pass and restored from HEAD~1 (see commit message).  ROOT CAUSE FOUND (code level, 2026-09-18 evening): the emitter is GitReins' OWN tier-2 evaluator. `engine/evaluator.py::_tool_run_command` ran the judge's shell as `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, timeout=...)` — `timeout=` reaps only the DIRECT child, so any BACKGROUNDED children escape: a command like `for i in $(seq 1 64); do timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c 'while :; do :; done' & done` (the idiom the judge invents when a criterion demands 'fails on a loaded box') leaves every unit running, reparented to `systemd --user`. Measured: 278 orphans, loadavg 220-346. ps chain proved the path: `gitreins task complete DF-CRIER-252` → the for-loop shell → the burners (a direct child of the gitreins process, which is why no Hermes session/tool-call record exists and why the terminal-jail veto does NOT cover it — the host reaper was the only backstop). Amplifiers: the tier-2 stage is budgeted at 400 iterations / 30m / 48M input tokens (crier/.gitreins/config.yaml), so a judge run is long and can issue many commands; crier's own criteria (e.g. QA-CRIER-17: '20+ consecutive go test ./cmd/server -count=1 runs are green') legitimately push the judge toward load-bearing verification. FIX LANDED: new `engine/command_hygiene.py` — (a) refuses busy-wait/unbounded-burn/fork-bomb commands with a message naming `sleep` and `scripts/loadgen.py`; (b) spawns every command with `start_new_session=True` and reaps the WHOLE process group on timeout AND on normal exit (validated pgid: never PID 1, group must exist in /proc, survivors are reported in the tool result rather than hidden). Wired into `_tool_run_command` and `pipeline._run_script_step`. Tests: `tests/test_command_hygiene.py`, 20 passing behaviour tests (backgrounded child reaped on normal exit; timeout kills the group; refusal proven by side effect). Deploy step: the lanes run the pipx copy at ~/.local/share/pipx/venvs/gitreins (installed from file:///home/kara/gitreins-poc), so it must be reinstalled from the repo for the fix to reach them.

title: [perf:P3] load-repro-selftest forks one `sed` per /proc entry per poll — it did not finish in 28 minutes on a 1.7k-process box, and the slow poll can miss the 2s premise it is trying to catch
detail: Measured in tick 341 on this host (1679 pids): scripts/load-repro-selftest.sh reached assertion 10 in ~3 min, then spent >25 min inside assertion 11 (SIGTERM-the-wrapper) without producing a verdict; the trace shows the /proc scan helpers (ppid_of/children_of) spawning `sed -n ... /proc/<pid>/status` once per pid, per poll tick, inside loops of 40-100 ticks. Two consequences: (1) a local verification of the harness on a fleet box is effectively unusable, and it also makes the CI step proportionally slower on a busy runner; (2) the premise assertion 11 depends on (generator alive with 2 burners + target alive) holds for only ~2s — the bounded fixture lifetime — while one poll tick can cost seconds at this process count, so the premise can be missed and the assertion fails as 'could not catch the run mid-flight in 2 attempts' on a loaded box even though the harness is correct. ACCEPTANCE: one snapshot pass per poll (a single python3 or awk read of the needed /proc fields, no per-pid fork), the fixture window documented or widened so the premise cannot be missed, and the whole selftest observed completing in < 60s on a host with > 1500 processes, with the timing recorded in the row. CI CONTEXT (added same tick): the same suite finishes in ~8s on a clean runner (run 35405142151, 15/15), so this is a fleet-box/local-verification defect first and a CI-runtime defect second; the premise-miss risk in assertion 11 is the part that can produce a false red on a loaded box.
reasoning: Picked as the freshest real defect on the board: it was filed by tick 341 against work that tick itself landed, so its acceptance criteria were already measured and falsifiable, and it had a live consequence on the fleet. Slowness evidence: tick 341 reached assertion 10 in ~3 min then spent >25 min inside assertion 11 without a verdict. measured wall time on this host (1730-1774 pids, 16 cpus): foreman's independent run `make load-repro-selftest` = 6.04s, exit 0, 15/15 assertions; the tier-2 judge's own two runs = 5.81s and 6.09s; the worker's four runs = 10.77 / 5.89 / 9.34 / 9.65s; worst observed 10.77s against the <60s budget. BEFORE, one legacy fork-per-pid pass = 6.38/7.24/6.84s at moderate load and 20.64/8.80/7.22s under loadavg 173; one live-oracle pass took 166.79s. True root cause discovered while foreman-verifying: this defect is ALSO what killed DF-CRIER-254's tier-2 judge — that judge ran `make load-repro-selftest` as its tier-1 evidence, the pre-fix scan never finished, and the eval died on the evaluator's 30m TIME cap (verdict da3fe4e0: 'Time cap (30m) exceeded (30m14s elapsed)'). The orphaned child processes survived that judge's exit by 33 minutes and were reaped by this tick (8 processes, one of them spawning a per-pid sed), which is why the judge's own re-runs of this selftest now finish in ~6s. JUDGE OUTCOME: the first tier-2 verdict (95094877) failed this row on ONE clause only — it required the measured wall time on the BOARD ROW and the row was still pending when the judge ran (clauses a-d passed, including the judge's own 5.81s/6.09s re-runs). After this row was written with the timings, `gitreins task complete DF-CRIER-256 --force` returned tier1 PASS, tier2 PASS (COMPLETE), Overall PASS — verdict b9d7317c, and the judge re-measured the suite at 5.56s/5.67s with 15/15 on a 1712-pid host.

title: [ci:P2] the bunker-matrix transport-retry classifier calls a `deadline_exceeded` stream error NON_TRANSPORT and dies with the retry budget unspent — bunker-e2e red on run 35408229089 (headSha 0914766, board-only diff)
detail: Measured 2026-09-18/19 (tick 342). bunker-e2e run 35408229089 (headSha 0914766, a board-JSONL-only commit — the diff cannot affect a container deploy) failed in job 'Bunker config-matrix E2E', step 'Deploy container to bunker + run config-matrix battery', during cell 'guard-on (default guard, real deepseek)' after `preflight OK`. Sequence from the log: image tarball -> bunker transport retried and succeeded ('attempt 1/4 (retry budget 3) -- OK'), 'docker load on <host>' retried and succeeded, THEN `bunker: stream error: deadline_exceeded: context deadline exceeded`, and the enclosing 'cell deploy: guard-on' leg reported: 'attempt 1/4 (retry budget 3 not spent — not retryable) — NON_TRANSPORT (exit 1; not a transport signature, output: sha256:74a271eae952015703d5a08ed369d74d501e977fe38a4a2d70682e78278fcfc4)' followed by FATAL. So a transport-shaped failure (a stream deadline) was classified NON_TRANSPORT, the budget of 3 retries was left UNSPENT, and the job died on the first attempt. The captured 'output' the classifier judged is the image sha256 line — the real signature ('deadline_exceeded', 'stream error') was on the line just before it, i.e. the classifier is reading the wrong line (or the wrong stream) of a multi-line attempt, so any cell deploy whose failure text is a stream error is unretryable. This is a follow-on to INT-CI-001 (commit 65aa127), which added exactly this retry+classify leg for the ssh/scp reset case and is complete — the classifier's signature set is what is incomplete, not the retry loop. Same run: the ghcr 'Build & publish image' job succeeded and pages succeeded; the previous two commits' bunker-e2e runs (713588f, c5386b6) both succeeded, which is why this reads as intermittent transport, not a code regression. ACCEPTANCE: a cell-deploy failure whose output contains a transport signature (deadline_exceeded / stream error / reset) is classified TRANSPORT and retried within the budget, proven by feeding the classifier the exact two-line attempt text from run 35408229089 in a test and observing a retry (and a deterministic NON_TRANSPORT verdict for a genuinely non-transport failure, e.g. a bad image ref); the classifier must read the WHOLE attempt output, not one captured line. Then re-run the bunker-e2e workflow and record the run id on this row.
